Read a neuroimaging color lookup table (LUT)

Source: R/read_lut.R
read_lut.Rd

Parses common neuroimaging atlas color lookup tables into a standardized tibble containing integer region values, text labels, RGB channels, and hex colors. The returned table can be passed directly to images(..., labels = lut) and scale_fill_lut().

Usage

read_lut(
  file,
  format = c("auto", "freesurfer", "itksnap", "fsl"),
  drop_zero = TRUE
)

Arguments

file

Path to a text color lookup table file.

format

Character string specifying the LUT format. One of:

  • "auto" (default): Detect format automatically from the header and first entry.

  • "freesurfer": Whitespace-delimited index label R G B [A] (e.g., FreeSurferColorLUT.txt, Yeo, or Schaefer LUTs).

  • "itksnap": ITK-SNAP label description format IDX R G B A VIS MSH "Label".

  • "fsl": FSL/FSLeyes label LUT format index R G B label (with RGB values in [0, 1] or [0, 255] and optional multi-word labels).

drop_zero

Logical; if TRUE (default), remove entries with value == 0 (typically background/unknown labels such as NONE, Unknown, or Clear Label), since ggbrain treats voxel value 0 as transparent background.

Value

A tibble with columns:

value

Integer ROI/parcel code matching values in the NIfTI atlas.

label

Character region or network name.

r, g, b

Integer RGB channel values in 0..255.

color

Hexadecimal RGB color string (e.g., "#781286").

See also

scale_fill_lut(), images()

Examples

lut_file <- system.file("extdata", "Yeo2011_7Networks_ColorLUT.txt", package = "ggbrain")
yeo_lut <- read_lut(lut_file)
yeo_lut
#> # A tibble: 7 × 6
#>   value label           r     g     b color  
#>   <int> <chr>       <int> <int> <int> <chr>  
#> 1     1 7Networks_1   120    18   134 #781286
#> 2     2 7Networks_2    70   130   180 #4682B4
#> 3     3 7Networks_3     0   118    14 #00760E
#> 4     4 7Networks_4   196    58   250 #C43AFA
#> 5     5 7Networks_5   220   248   164 #DCF8A4
#> 6     6 7Networks_6   230   148    34 #E69422
#> 7     7 7Networks_7   205    62    78 #CD3E4E
